### Why this is needed

By default, the DAGs search in the Airflow UI uses a fast prefix search. Users can toggle the "match anywhere" (substring search) button to refine their queries. However, this toggle state was previously only stored in `localStorage`. 

This created a major usability gap: if a user filtered the DAGs list using "match anywhere" and shared that URL with a colleague, the recipient wouldn't see the same results unless they coincidentally had the "match anywhere" toggle enabled in their own browser's local storage.

---

### How this solves the problem

This PR introduces the `match_anywhere` URL parameter to properly persist the toggle state, ensuring reproducible and shareable deep links.

*   **Selective Persistence**: We modified the `useAdvancedSearch` React hook to optionally accept a URL parameter key. This allows the DAGs list search to sync with the URL without polluting the URL state for all other search bars across the UI.
*   **Deep Linking**: The toggle now reads its initial state from the `match_anywhere` query parameter (falling back to local storage if absent). When toggled, it dynamically adds or removes `?match_anywhere=true` from the URL.

---

### What is unique about this implementation

Rather than globally coupling the `useAdvancedSearch` hook to the URL—which would have forced *all* search inputs across the application (like XComs, Task Instances, Events, etc.) to inject "match anywhere" states into the URL—we implemented a highly targeted approach. 

The hook now accepts an optional `searchParamKey` argument. By creating a new strongly-typed `MATCH_ANYWHERE` property in the `SearchParamsKeys` enum and passing it strictly to the DAGs list component, we preserve the default clean URL behavior for the rest of the application while explicitly solving the deep-linking requirement for the DAGs list.

closes: #73772

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
The substring ("match anywhere") search toggle only persisted in each browser's localStorage, so a filtered search could not be reproduced from a shared link — a colleague opening the URL saw prefix-only results unless they happened to have the same toggle enabled locally (#73772).

This mirrors the toggle in a shareable `match_anywhere` URL param. It is a repeated param listing the searchbars whose toggle is on (e.g. `?match_anywhere=dag_id&match_anywhere=run_id`), so pages with several independent text filters stay unambiguous. A key present in the URL wins so a shared link reproduces the sender's results; otherwise the existing per-searchbar localStorage preference still applies, and toggling the control writes both.

The change is a single central tweak to the `useAdvancedSearch` hook, so every searchbar and per-filter toggle that already uses it is covered uniformly. No visual change — the existing toggle now just reflects into, and reads back from, the URL.

closes: #73772

issue.body:
**Stacked on #74019** — that PR (persisting the match-anywhere toggle in the URL) is the first commit here; review/merge it first. This PR adds the second commit.

Turning on substring ("match anywhere") search has to be redone on every searchbar today, since the toggle only remembers itself per searchbar. This adds a single **Settings → Search → "Match anywhere by default"** switch so a user can opt into substring search everywhere at once.

Resolution order for any searchbar becomes: a key in the `match_anywhere` URL param wins (shareable), then the user's explicit per-searchbar choice (localStorage), then this global default, then prefix. So a shared link and a manually-set filter still take precedence over the default. The helper text calls out that substring search is slower because it cannot use the prefix index.
